title: Hong Kong Arts Festival Society says its website was accessed by an unauthorized third party; data of thousands of ticket bookers may be affected
date_note: RTHK, published 2026-11-26, says the society announced it on Monday; resolved to 23 November. The page gives no earlier date for the intrusion itself.
geo_basis: Society based in Hong Kong, as the RTHK report states; no street address given
summary: The Hong Kong Arts Festival Society said in a statement, reported by RTHK, that its main website was accessed by an unauthorized third party. It preliminarily suspects the personal data of thousands of ticket-booking audience members for the 55th festival may have been illegally viewed. The society says it reported to police and the privacy commissioner and sent email notices to possibly affected people.
plain: The Hong Kong Arts Festival says an unauthorized party accessed its website. It suspects the data of thousands of people who booked tickets may have been viewed, and says it has told police and the privacy commissioner.
exec: The society says personal data of thousands of ticket bookers may have been viewed; it has reported to police and the privacy commissioner.
action: The Hong Kong Arts Festival Society says it emailed possibly affected audience members; follow the notice it sent.

sources.name: RTHK Chinese: Hong Kong Arts Festival website intrusion

validation.note: One publisher read (RTHK), quoting the society's own statement; the society's statement itself was not read.
